name: Apple
one_liner: Builds iPhone, Mac, iOS, iCloud, Siri and Apple silicon; interviews are run by the hiring team, vary widely, and weigh domain depth and 'Why Apple?'.

levels.intern: Software Engineering Intern or co-op (summer internships or academic-year co-ops; official students page: 'open to those enrolled full-time and pursuing a bachelor's degree, master's degree, or doctorate'). India: IS&T intern roles are reported (e.g. Reliability Engineering IS&T Intern, Oct 2025, offer the next day); duration and PPO terms are not confirmed in sources. Apple's internship search listed 89 results on Oct 4, 2026; the newest were mostly in Europe and China.
levels.new_grad: ICT2 ('Junior Software Engineer' on Levels.fyi). Posting titles seen in 2025 to 2026 reports: 'Software Engineer, IS&T Early Career' (US, Aug 2026) and 'Junior Software Engineer' (India, for freshers, Aug 2025).
levels.early_career: ICT2 to ICT3 ('Software Engineer'); Levels.fyi ICT3 data points start at about 2 YOE. Level is set by the hiring team after the loop.

process_new_grad.stage: Apply to a specific team posting
process_new_grad.details: There is no central Apple loop: you apply to a team's requisition on jobs.apple.com and the recruiter and interviewers belong to that team (Aced, interviewing.io). Shortlisting is team-specific, so tailor your resume to each posting (Mar 2025 ICT3 report). You can interview with several teams at once (interviewing.io).
15 to 30 min recruiter call (background, why Apple, compensation expectations), sometimes followed by a hiring manager conversation that can include technical questions (Aced).

Used by some teams, not all. Reported formats: 2 coding problems in 60 to 70 min on CoderPad or a similar platform (IS&T SWE Hyderabad, May 2025: Java-only, 70 min; India Junior SWE for freshers, Aug 2025: Java-only; Junior SWE ICT2, Aug 2025: Java or Python), sometimes plus 15 to 20 MCQs on the role's stack (Jan 2025 OA: 2 coding + 15 MCQ; IC3 Frontend, Jun 2025: 1 hour, 2 coding + 20 JavaScript/React MCQs).

1 to 2 interviews of 45 to 60 min, usually on CoderPad: DSA plus CS fundamentals or language depth. A US IS&T Early Career candidate (Aug 2026) was told by the recruiter to expect 'a quick intro, CS fundamentals, and around 15 minutes of coding'. A Java backend role for 0 to 3 years (Feb 2026) scheduled a 60-min CoderPad round on Core Java, data structures and problem solving. India IS&T rounds mix DSA with Java, Spring Boot, OOP and microservices theory.

Virtual or in person, about 3 to 8 rounds depending on team (Aced blog: 3 to 8 rounds of 45 to 60 min; interviewing.io: 6 to 8; Aced guide: 4 to 7 rounds counting screens): coding, domain (iOS, frontend, backend, systems), sometimes LLD or design, and a hiring manager or behavioral round centered on 'Why Apple?'. India Junior SWE for freshers (Aug 2025): DSA round, Java/Python/microservices/LLD round, techno-managerial round.

Teams decide in live debriefs; the hiring manager has the most influence (interviewing.io). Offers then need approvals, which can take weeks: an ICT3 candidate (Mar 2025) wrote that Apple 'requires 4 levels of signatures up to the VP level to roll out the offer'; a Jun 2025 candidate had a verbal offer with the written offer 'pending business approvals' for over 3 weeks. Some candidates are told after the loop that the position was filled by someone else (IC3 Frontend, Jun 2025).

process_intern.details: Search 'Students: Internships' on jobs.apple.com; postings are team-specific and appear through the year (Summer 2027 GPU intern postings appeared Aug and Sep 2026 per prior verification).

Usually 1 to 2 team interviews of about 45 min (an Apple Vision Pro intern candidate in Mar 2025 was scheduled for one 45-min interview); expect coding plus project discussion, but US intern reports are sparse.

Round 1 technical elimination (about 50 min): project deep dive, CoderPad DSA (rotate matrix, merge k sorted lists, longest mountain, LRU cache design), complexity theory and networking (DNS, TCP vs UDP, caching, L1/L2/L3 cache). Shortlist email within 30 min. Round 2 managerial and HR (about 50 min): 5 to 6 behavioral questions each on Collaboration, Invention and Results. Offer reported the next day.

process_experienced_notes: With 1 to 3 years (ICT3 range), expect a recruiter or HM screen, 1 to 2 technical screens, then 3 to 6 onsite rounds: coding, language internals (Java concurrency, Spring Boot, React hooks), LLD, and a team-specific system design (BookMyShow, TinyURL, distributed rate limiter; a Senior Systems Engineer reported fraud detection with rate limiters). Questions about how you use GenAI tools appear in 2025 to 2026 screens (Hyderabad Ads Delivery, Nov 2025; Hyderabad SWE offer, May 2026). One Sep 2026 report (9 YOE Java role) lists an 'AI assisted coding round' in the loop; Aced (Oct 2026) says Apple 'hasn't announced or adopted the AI-assisted coding rounds that Meta and Google have started piloting', and interviewing.io says AI use is prohibited, so treat AI rounds as team experiments and ask your recruiter.
timeline: Aced: 4 to 8 weeks in most cases, up to 3 to 4 months; long gaps between stages are common. Aced blog: anywhere from 3 weeks to 4 months. After a verbal offer, written offers can wait on approvals and headcount checks. Apple hires year-round by team rather than in a single new grad season.

oa.platform: Varies by team: CoderPad link or HackerRank-style assessment; many US teams skip the OA and start with a recruiter or hiring manager screen
oa.format: Commonly 2 coding problems in 60 to 70 min (examples: two-bag knapsack, follow a path through a 15 x 10 grid), sometimes plus 15 to 20 MCQs on the team's stack (JavaScript/React, Java)
oa.notes: Language may be fixed by the team (Java-only OAs reported for IS&T India). Difficulty easy to medium; time is the main constraint.

coding.rounds: 1 to 3 technical screens plus 1 to 3 onsite coding rounds (Aced); team-dependent
coding.style: Medium LeetCode-style problems plus practical, team-mapped tasks: implement a data structure (thread-safe LRU, HashMap), Java concurrency, React components (nested tabs, rendering 1M rows), vague prompts that you must scope. Interviewers write their own questions; there is no central question bank (Aced, interviewing.io).
coding.environment: Mostly CoderPad (copy-paste often blocked); some teams use your own laptop and IDE or a take-home assignment; FaceTime/Zoom or in person. Plan to work without AI unless told otherwise.
coding.graded_on: Working, dry-run code; data structure choice; core language depth; trade-off reasoning; communication; fit with the team's domain. Hiring manager weight is high and behavioral signal matters as much as coding for many teams (interviewing.io).

system_design: Rare for ICT2 new grads and interns, though IS&T intern candidates ask about HLD/LLD basics and India junior loops include an LLD-flavored round. ICT3 and above get team-specific design focused on reliability, privacy and on-device vs cloud trade-offs (Aced; interviewing.io notes Apple interviewers 'love to hear about reliability').

behavioral.framework: No published interview framework; team-run behavioral and hiring manager rounds built around 'Why Apple?', collaboration, invention and results; Apple's shared values (accessibility, privacy, environment, inclusion)
what_they_look_for: A genuine, specific 'Why Apple?' and why this team (asked repeatedly)
Passion for Apple products tied to your own story
Collaboration across teams with limited guidance
Invention: original solutions in your projects
Depth on your own projects and technical decisions
Discretion and comfort with a secretive, siloed culture
How you use GenAI tools day to day (2025 to 2026 screens)
sample_questions: Walk me through your resume and the work you are most proud of.
Tell me about a time you worked in a team without sufficient guidance.
Tell me about a time you came up with an innovative solution in a project.
Tell me about a time you had a setback and still delivered.
Tell me about a time you had a disagreement with a peer.
Tell me about a time you delivered in a short time and reprioritized work.
What GenAI tools do you use day to day, and how do they improve your efficiency?
Given Apple values like deep expertise and drive for excellence, how have you shown them in your career?

non_leetcode_formats: Domain deep dives in the team's stack (iOS, React output prediction and hooks, Java/Spring Boot theory, OS and networking fundamentals); take-home assignments chosen by the hiring manager (interviewing.io); presenting a past project (Aced blog); code review or design-pattern refactoring in an LLD round (Sep 2026 report); vague, scoped-by-you prompts such as a vote counter that must batch millions of ballots.

tips: Ask your recruiter forced-choice questions about each round (LeetCode-style vs domain deep dive, which language) because every team runs its own loop (interviewing.io).
Prepare a specific 'Why Apple, why this team' story tied to products you use; some interviewers reject on this alone (interviewing.io).
Study the team's stack in depth: Java concurrency and Spring for IS&T backend roles, React hooks and DOM for frontend, Swift and iOS for app teams.
Apply to several Apple teams at once; you can run parallel processes.
Practice medium problems on CoderPad with copy-paste off and dry-run your own tests.
For India IS&T internships, revise CS fundamentals (networking, DNS, caching, OS, DBMS) along with DSA and your projects.
Expect delays between rounds and after a verbal offer; follow up politely and keep other processes alive.
Do not plan on AI help in interviews; confirm the rules with your recruiter.
compensation_note: Levels.fyi (fetched Oct 4, 2026), US Software Engineer ICT2: average total comp $166,692 from only 14 recent data points; p25 $152,820, median $161,000, p75 $175,000 (page range $145K to $191K+); median base $140,234, median stock $22,500/yr. ICT3: average $255,770 (41 data points). Small ICT2 sample: treat as a rough range. An ICT3 full-stack offer (Mar 2025, Cupertino) was reported as $175K base, $33K/yr stock, $20K sign-on, 7.5% bonus.
